reviews.review: Been playing Arma 3 for a few years now. Highly recommend this game because it has so many uses via the multiplayer game modes.
Nice Game and The Best Life Game
Played a couple of hours... It was alright, I guess.
If you are more of a singleplayer person I can recommend a mod called Pilgrimage. I have had a lot of fun with that mission.

Now let me start this off by saying that Arma is a game like no other, its own universe practically, filled with thousands of "worlds" created by players and modders. And i really do like the game, i just can't actually recommend it. Playing Arma 3 is like eating a great sandwich, that also happens to have bells hanging from it, and every time the bell rings someone scratches metal nails down a chalkboard. The sandwich tastes amazing, but in no way justifies the incessant annoyance, and you'll find yourself thinking about all the great things the sandwich could be.

To list a few "bells":
>OPTIMIZATION: The game feels incredibly clunky, and is quite possibly the most un-optimized game i've ever played. It's fine on GPU's but wont use enough of your CPU to make it run smoothly.
>CPU INTENSIVE: Framerate is tough, you have to do a hell of a lot of self optimization with settings and so much testing to even get a smooth consistent framerate, but then the second you put in actual AI soldiers and they have to start thinking(or really anything other than the player), it'll spike your framerate into the ground like an NFL player spikes their fist into their wife. There are literally HUNDREDS of videos on youtube that try to offer optimization for actually playable framerate. Even if you COULD handle a full scale battle while remaining at 60FPS, there will be completely random framerate drops with no logical explanation, lended by the horrible lack of optimization. It's all CPU, graphics aren't even a problem. I have an AMD RX 580 and can run the game on high settings with a smooth 60fps framerate, yet the moment i enter a medium-large scale scenario it immediately begins running like 25FPS, on low or high settings.
>BALLISTICS SIMULATION: Now it's totally awesome how ARMA keeps track of everything and runs realistic simulations on things in the background, totally cool! Except that when you're 100 meters away from an enemy, and place a high velocity round just above his head accounting for a slight drop, it'll go straight over his head like the obvious lies your girlfriend tells you when she goes out to cheat on you. Now take the same scenario and actually aim at his head, and the round will drop to like his throat/collarbone area. What? Now clearly there are people who are very accustomed to Arma 3 hitboxes, as i've been Lynx'd from over 700 meters in KoTH games, but I've played almost 400 hours and as accustomed to it as i am, i find i'm STILL not nearly accustomed enough with the ballistics simulation to pull off impressively long shots. Now i'll be clear the ACE mod has it's own ballistics simulation which is far better, so this can be fixed with mods, but not every scenario or server is compatible, so eventually you'll have to suffer missing someone who's 100 meters away while aiming center mass, while also being hit from almost 1km.
>UNREASONABLE DLC: So picture this, you just found an amazing scenario you want to try, you download the mods required, start the ♥♥♥♥♥ up, and begin your game. You're immediately confronted with this annoying message in the bottom right corner saying you're wearing a DLC item! Like oh, okay cool thanks for telling me. But wait! 30 seconds later a grayscale pattern with something akin to "Arma 3: Laws of War DLC" written a million times descends over your ENTIRE screen! it disappears about 30 seconds later to show you you're running into a wall like a short bus kid who's helmet fell over their eyes, and then you get a new message! An opaque pop-up directly in the middle of your screen telling you "Hey, buy the DLC and the messages will go away!" So you check it out and it's $7 for a pack of a few clothing items and a drone. This happens with weapons, vehicles, anything DLC. OR it will just not allow you to use it at all. Many scenarios are created with DLC content because they provide either beefed up or enhanced versions of basically what's already basegame content. It gets frustrating, and I've actually (regrettedly so) purchased 3 of the DLC packs. What a waste of money.
>DESYNCING: De-synchronization for you special types. Player bodies, even player driven vehicles, will randomly stop as the server/game takes a quick smoke break, only for you to crash into it or be blocked by a body, and then resync to catch up to wherever the object is now. It will actually treat your game as if you've hit a stationary object, even though it's driving at 100km/h or running full speed.
>CLIPPING: Now this may be the most frustrating aspect of MP, even SP gameplay. F*cking clipping. You'll be in an intense KoTH game, the AO is tied up and you've been defending a tower for almost an entire hour now, fending it off. You're in the corner of the tower, and you go prone to make a smaller target, and turn to the right to get your sights on the doo- OH and you've magically no-clipped through the wall and are now falling 50 meters to your death. That's just an example, this game has SUCH a big problem with clipping, assumedly from the 5th grade optimization done on static objects and props. You can even clip into unaccessable areas of the map (i.e Closed shipping container) and be stuck until you respawn or take a bite out of your own grenade.
>UNFIXABLE CODE: Say you're a code savvy gent/gentess, and you decide to take a quick peek at the game system code to straighten a few things up. Guess what! You'll be sent an email by bohemia interactive threatening lawsuits for trying to fix their code.
>LEARNING CURVE: If you want to play this game to it's full extent you can't just jump into it like any other game and start playing. You have to teach yourself the keybindings (There's about the same amount of keybindings as there are sperm cells on a motel bedsheet), you have to teach yourself the physics of the game to ensure you don't kill yourself and your squad constantly, you have to teach yourself how to be legitimately tactical because you'll get popped by an AI 400 meters away before you even know you were within 5 clicks of an enemy, and GOD FORBID YOU WANT TO MAKE A MISSION, you better teach yourself some serious sh*t.
>MISSION MAKING: Had to give this one it's own category just because of HOW MUCH of a learning curve their is. If you want to make a simple two-sided mission, there's all of these different vague modules that are basically packages of codes compressed into a placeable "object" that you need to physically put in game, with little to no explanation of what they actually are, do, or how to use them. There are like a combined 100,000+ hours (most likely not exaggerated) of youtube videos that explain how to use them, but only in very specific scenarios, most of which will never actually match what you want to do with them. If you want to make anything other than a plain, barebones scenario, you need to know how to code. Not some crazy I-Just-Hacked-Into-The-Pentagon coding, but basic knowledge of how coding works, and then you have to teach yourself all of the SPECIFIC Arma syntaxes and codes and commands and how to use them together, how to edit files, basically you'll spend twice as much time learning as you'll spend playing the game. I have probably about 100+hours in the editor, and 50+hours of teaching myself these things, and still have yielded nothing more than small 10 minute scenarios with very basic gameplay.
>OVERAMBITIOUS: To sum things up the game is straight a classic case of overambition. There's so many amazing sounding features and things to do that they all get in the way of eachother and none are completely working at all.

Now I've left a lot out because I've already written a lot and i'm hitting the text cap, but I'll say that the Community is the most amazing part of this game, and id say the best out of any game. The inherent complicity of Arma makes paint-eaters despise it, so mods, scenarios, and teammates, are usually really good. I'd love to elaborate more on some good things but I've hit the text cap.
